title: Advancement vs acceleration: target-aware selection under a train-target gap
setting: Teacher-student binary classification with 20-d Gaussian inputs: a pool is labeled by a source teacher, while evaluation uses fresh samples labeled by a target teacher rotated by a gap angle (optionally with label noise). An L2-regularized logistic regression is fit to convergence on the pool (uncurated), on a random half, or on a half selected using a probe trained on 40 labeled target examples (drops target-conflicting labels, keeps near-boundary points). The metric is accuracy on 4000 fresh target samples against clean target labels.

paper.title: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training
paper.claim: Curation improves the attainable (converged) target performance only when there is a correctable train-target gap (Delta > 0); with no gap it cannot beat the uncurated baseline at large budget.

metric.name: target_acc
metric.description: Accuracy on fresh target-distribution samples (clean target-teacher labels) of the model trained on the chosen data. Diagnostics: target_logloss, baseline_target_acc, delta_test (|target loss - train loss| of the uncurated model), n_kept.

factors.name: method
factors.description: uniform: train on the full pool; target_select: keep half the pool chosen with a probe fit on a small labeled target set; random_select: keep a random half (controls for the loss of sample size).

factors.name: gap_deg
factors.description: Angle in degrees between source and target teachers (train-target gap); 0 means train and target objectives coincide.

factors.name: n_pool
factors.description: Pool size, standing in for the training budget; larger pools approach the converged endpoint.

factors.name: label_noise
factors.description: Probability of flipping labels in the pool and in the small labeled target set; noise makes the target probe less reliable.
